120th Congress 

To provide pathways to prosperity by expanding economic opportunity, reducing regulatory barriers, promoting workforce development, supporting small businesses, reforming education, and empowering individuals and families to achieve self-reliance and break the cycle of poverty, and for other purposes.

IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

Dr. Báez (for himself and cosponsors) introduced the following bill, which was referred to the Committee on Education and the Workforce, Ways and Means, Energy and Commerce, Small Business, and Financial Services. 

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE; TABLE OF CONTENTS.

(a) Short Title. This Act may be cited as the “Prosperity Through Opportunity Act.”

(b) Table of Contents. The table of contents for this Act is as follows:

Sec. 1. Short title; table of contents.
Sec. 2. Findings and purpose.
Sec. 3. Definitions.

TITLE I: WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND JOB TRAINING
TITLE II: SMALL BUSINESS AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP SUPPORT
TITLE III: EDUCATION REFORM AND SCHOOL CHOICE
TITLE IV: TAX INCENTIVES AND REGULATORY RELIEF
TITLE V: FAMILY AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT
TITLE VI: ADMINISTRATION AND FUNDING

SECTION 2. FINDINGS AND PURPOSE.

(a) Findings. Congress finds the following:

(1) Persistent poverty in districts such as Texas’s 20th Congressional District stems not from a lack of government spending, but from barriers to opportunity, including failing public schools, excessive regulations, high taxes, family breakdown, and government dependency fostered by socialist-style policies.

(2) The American Dream is rooted in personal responsibility, free enterprise, faith, family, and hard work. Historical data show that education, stable two-parent families, full-time work, and avoidance of dependency are the strongest predictors of escaping poverty.

(3) Overregulation and bureaucratic red tape disproportionately harm low-income entrepreneurs and small businesses, which create the majority of new jobs.

(4) School choice and vocational training have proven effective in empowering families and preparing workers for high-demand careers.

(5) Targeted, pro-growth tax policies and regulatory relief, rather than expansive welfare programs, drive sustained economic mobility.

(b) Purpose. The purpose of this Act is to: 

(1) Expand economic opportunity by removing barriers to work, entrepreneurship, and upward mobility;

(2) Promote self-reliance, personal responsibility, and family stability;

(3) Reform education systems to prioritize skills, literacy, and workforce readiness over ideological indoctrination;

(4) Support small businesses and innovation in high-poverty communities;

(5) Reduce government dependency while protecting those truly in need; and

(6) Align federal policy with constitutional principles, limited government, and the values of faith-informed service to our communities.

SECTION 3. DEFINITIONS.

In this Act:

(1) Opportunity Zone. The term has the meaning given in section 1400Z-1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

(2) Eligible Entity. Includes States, local governments, community colleges, trade schools, nonprofit organizations with proven track records of job placement (excluding those primarily engaged in advocacy), and faith-based organizations.

(3) Self-Reliance Metric. A measurement developed by the Secretary of Labor, in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, that tracks exits from means-tested welfare programs, employment retention, wage growth, and family stability.

TITLE I: WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND JOB TRAINING

SEC. 101. EXPANSION OF WORKFORCE INNOVATION AND OPPORTUNITY ACT (WIOA) FLEXIBILITY.

(a) States shall receive block grants under WIOA with greater flexibility to prioritize apprenticeships, on-the-job training, and industry-recognized credentials over classroom-only programs.

(b) At least 60 percent of funds must demonstrate measurable outcomes in job placement and wage gains within 6 months.

SEC. 102. NATIONAL APPRENTICESHIP INCENTIVE PROGRAM.

(a) Establishes a tax credit of up to $5,000 per apprentice for employers who hire and retain individuals from high-poverty census tracts for registered apprenticeships in trades, manufacturing, healthcare, technology, and infrastructure.

(b) Prioritizes veterans, former foster youth, and individuals exiting the criminal justice system.

SEC. 103. VOCATIONAL EDUCATION GRANTS.

Authorizes $500,000,000 annually for competitive grants to community colleges and trade schools partnering with employers for short-term, high-return certification programs (e.g., welding, HVAC, nursing, coding, commercial driving).

SEC. 104. BAN ON USE OF FUNDS FOR IDEOLOGICAL TRAINING.

No funds under this title may support programs that include diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) mandates, gender ideology, or critical race theory content.

TITLE II: SMALL BUSINESS AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP SUPPORT

SEC. 201. MICRO-LOAN AND MENTORSHIP EXPANSION.

(a) Increases funding and eligibility for Small Business Administration microloans (up to $100,000) targeted at Opportunity Zones and high-poverty areas.

(b) Requires mentorship components through partnerships with SCORE, chambers of commerce, and faith-based organizations.

SEC. 202. REGULATORY RELIEF FOR SMALL BUSINESSES.

(a) Exempts businesses with fewer than 50 employees from certain federal regulations for the first 3 years of operation.

(b) Creates a “One-Stop Shop” federal portal for permitting and compliance assistance.

SEC. 203. NEW MARKETS TAX CREDIT EXTENSION AND EXPANSION.

Permanently extends and increases the New Markets Tax Credit with a focus on job-creating projects in distressed communities.

TITLE III: EDUCATION REFORM AND SCHOOL CHOICE

SEC. 301. FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE TAX CREDIT.

Creates a refundable tax credit for contributions to scholarship organizations that provide K-12 education savings accounts, enabling low-income families to choose private, public charter, homeschool, or vocational options.

SEC. 302. ACCOUNTABILITY FOR FAILING SCHOOLS.

(a) Withholds federal education funds from persistently failing Title I schools (as measured by NAEP and graduation rates) unless they implement proven reforms, including phonics-based reading, core skills curriculum, and removal of ideological content.

(b) Strengthens parental rights notification and opt-out provisions.

SEC. 303. CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION MODERNIZATION.

Reauthorizes and reforms Perkins CTE with emphasis on industry partnerships and measurable employment outcomes.

TITLE IV: TAX INCENTIVES AND REGULATORY RELIEF

SEC. 401. EARNED INCOME TAX CREDIT ENHANCEMENT FOR WORKERS.

Increases the EITC for full-time workers in high-poverty areas while adding work requirements and phase-outs to encourage upward mobility.

SEC. 402. CAPITAL GAINS EXCLUSION FOR INVESTMENTS IN DISTRESSED COMMUNITIES.

Provides a 100% capital gains exclusion for qualified investments held for 5+ years in Opportunity Zones or designated high-poverty areas.

SEC. 403. PERMANENT FULL EXPENSING AND IMMEDIATE R&D DEDUCTION.

Extends pro-growth tax provisions to stimulate business investment and innovation.

SEC. 404. REDUCTION IN FEDERAL REGULATORY BURDEN.

Directs agencies to repeal two existing regulations for every new one issued, with a moratorium on new major rules affecting small businesses in high-poverty districts.

TITLE V: FAMILY AND COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT

SEC. 501. MARRIAGE AND FAMILY INCENTIVES.

(a) Provides enhanced child tax credits for married couples.

(b) Funds evidence-based programs promoting family stability and responsible fatherhood through community and faith-based organizations.

SEC. 502. COMMUNITY REINVESTMENT THROUGH FAITH AND LOCAL PARTNERS.

Prioritizes funding for proven, locally led initiatives by churches, nonprofits, and civic groups that deliver job training, mentoring, addiction recovery, and financial literacy with measurable self-reliance outcomes.

SEC. 503. SECOND CHANCE AND REENTRY SUPPORT.

Expands proven reentry programs focused on work, mentorship, and accountability rather than expanded entitlements.

TITLE VI: ADMINISTRATION AND FUNDING

SEC. 601. OFFICE OF OPPORTUNITY AND SELF-RELIANCE.

Establishes an interagency office within the Department of Commerce to coordinate implementation and annual reporting on self-reliance metrics.

SEC. 602. AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.

There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act for fiscal years 2027 through 2032, subject to annual appropriations and performance-based renewals.

IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

Dr. Edgardo Rafael Báez, Representative for Texas’s 20th Congressional District, introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Homeland Security, in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, Education and the Workforce, Veterans’ Affairs, and Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

A BILL 

To protect American families and communities by securing the sovereignty of the United States, restoring law and order, safeguarding children from violence and exploitation, supporting veterans and first responders, and defending the constitutional rights of law-abiding citizens.

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE; TABLE OF CONTENTS.

(a) Short Title. This Act may be cited as the “American Families and Communities Protection Act” or the “AFCPA.”

(b) Table of Contents. The table of contents for this Act is as follows:

Sec. 1. Short title; table of contents.
Sec. 2. Findings and purpose.
Sec. 3. Definitions.

TITLE I: BORDER SECURITY AND INTERIOR ENFORCEMENT
TITLE II: LAW AND ORDER AND PUBLIC SAFETY
TITLE III: CHILD AND FAMILY PROTECTION
TITLE IV: VETERANS AND FIRST RESPONDERS PROTECTION
TITLE V: ENFORCEMENT AND OVERSIGHT
TITLE VI: GENERAL PROVISIONS

SECTION 2. FINDINGS AND PURPOSE.

(a) Findings. Congress finds the following:

(1) The security of the United States border is a fundamental responsibility of the Federal Government under Article IV, Section 4 of the Constitution.

(2) Unprecedented levels of illegal immigration, fentanyl trafficking, and transnational gang activity have resulted in thousands of American deaths annually, strained public resources, and eroded community safety, particularly in border States and districts like Texas’s 20th Congressional District.

(3) American families have the right to raise their children in environments free from violence, exploitation, and ideological indoctrination that undermines parental authority and traditional values.

(4) Law enforcement officers, first responders, and veterans who have sacrificed for this Nation deserve unwavering support and protection from both physical threats and bureaucratic neglect.

(5) The right of law-abiding citizens to keep and bear arms, as guaranteed by the Second Amendment, must be vigorously protected against Federal overreach.

(6) Effective protection requires accountability, transparency, and the prioritization of American citizens and legal residents.

(b) Purpose. The purpose of this Act is to deliver decisive, comprehensive protections to American families and communities through strengthened borders, restored law and order, child safety measures, veteran support, and constitutional safeguards.

SECTION 3. DEFINITIONS.

In this Act:

The term “alien” has the meaning given to such term in section 101(a)(3) of the Immigration and Nationality Act.
The term “criminal gang” includes organizations designated under section 110 of title 18, United States Code, or successor provisions.

The term “parental rights” includes the fundamental right to direct the upbringing, education, and moral instruction of one’s children, as recognized by the Supreme Court.

Additional terms shall be defined consistent with existing Federal statutes.

TITLE I: BORDER SECURITY AND INTERIOR ENFORCEMENT

SEC. 101. COMPLETION OF PHYSICAL BORDER BARRIER.

The Secretary of Homeland Security, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, shall complete construction of not fewer than 700 miles of reinforced physical barriers, sensors, and surveillance technology along the southern border within 24 months of enactment. Priority shall be given to high-traffic smuggling zones.

SEC. 102. MANDATORY DETENTION AND EXPEDITED REMOVAL.

All aliens apprehended after unlawful entry shall be detained pending removal or credible fear determination. Expedited removal procedures under section 235(b) of the Immigration and Nationality Act shall be expanded to apply nationwide.

SEC. 103. PROHIBITION ON CATCH-AND-RELEASE.

No alien shall be released into the interior of the United States pending adjudication of immigration status unless the alien demonstrates lawful presence and passes comprehensive background checks. Release shall require approval by the Attorney General.

SEC. 104. PENALTIES FOR ILLEGAL REENTRY AND SMUGGLING.

Section 276 of the Immigration and Nationality Act is amended to impose a mandatory minimum sentence of 5 years for illegal reentry after prior removal, with enhanced penalties for those involved in smuggling or trafficking.

SEC. 105. DESIGNATION OF CARTELS AS TERRORIST ORGANIZATIONS.

Not later than 90 days after enactment, the Secretary of State shall designate major Mexican and Central American drug cartels and transnational criminal organizations as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, enabling full application of counterterrorism authorities.

SEC. 106. E-VERIFY MANDATE AND WORKPLACE ENFORCEMENT.

All employers with more than 10 employees shall utilize the E-Verify system. Civil and criminal penalties for knowingly employing unauthorized aliens are increased.

TITLE II: LAW AND ORDER AND PUBLIC SAFETY

SEC. 201. RESTORATION OF MANDATORY MINIMUMS.

Mandatory minimum sentences are reinstated for Federal crimes involving violence, firearms, fentanyl distribution resulting in death, and repeat serious offenders.

SEC. 202. SUPPORT FOR STATE AND LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT.

$5,000,000,000 is authorized for Byrne JAG and COPS grants to hire officers, acquire equipment, and support training, with eligibility conditioned on full cooperation with Federal immigration detainers.

SEC. 203. TRANSNATIONAL GANG TASK FORCES.

The Attorney General shall establish permanent multi-jurisdictional task forces targeting MS-13, Tren de Aragua, and similar gangs, with enhanced RICO and conspiracy penalties.

SEC. 204. PROTECTION OF SECOND AMENDMENT RIGHTS.

No Federal funds may be used for national firearms registration, red-flag confiscations without full due process (including notice, hearing, and counsel), or any infringement on the rights of law-abiding citizens.

SEC. 205. PENALTIES FOR ATTACKS ON LAW ENFORCEMENT.

Assaults on Federal, State, or local law enforcement officers resulting in serious injury shall carry a mandatory minimum of 10 years imprisonment.

TITLE III: CHILD AND FAMILY PROTECTION

SEC. 301. SCHOOL SAFETY AND PARENTAL NOTIFICATION.

All public schools receiving Federal funds shall implement immediate parental notification protocols for any violent incident, threat, or disciplinary action involving a child. Hardened school security grants are authorized, prioritizing resource officers.

SEC. 302. SAFEGUARDING CHILDREN FROM EXPLOITATION.

Federal education funds are withheld from States that permit the exposure of minors to sexually explicit content or gender ideology instruction without explicit, informed parental consent. Parental rights to opt out and review curriculum are guaranteed.

SEC. 303. ENHANCED PENALTIES FOR CHILD TRAFFICKING AND EXPLOITATION.

Mandatory minimum sentences of 25 years to life imprisonment are established for aggravated child sex trafficking, online enticement, and related offenses under chapters 77 and 110 of title 18, United States Code.

SEC. 304. FAMILY UNITY IN IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT.

Priority in removal proceedings shall be given to aliens with criminal records or recent unlawful entry, while protecting the unity of United States citizen families.

TITLE IV: VETERANS AND FIRST RESPONDERS PROTECTION

SEC. 401. EXPEDITED VETERANS’ BENEFITS AND HEALTHCARE.

The Department of Veterans Affairs shall prioritize claims processing for combat veterans and those with service-connected disabilities, with full benefits extended to training and deployment-related conditions.

SEC. 402. ANTI-FRAUD MEASURES FOR VETERANS PROGRAMS.

Criminal penalties are increased for benefits fraud, and a dedicated Inspector General task force is established.

SEC. 403. SUPPORT FOR FIRST RESPONDERS.

Tax credits, enhanced workers’ compensation, and mental health resources are authorized for law enforcement officers, firefighters, and emergency medical personnel injured or traumatized in the line of duty.

TITLE V: ENFORCEMENT AND OVERSIGHT

SEC. 501. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS.

The Secretary of Homeland Security and Attorney General shall submit quarterly reports to Congress detailing border encounters, removal statistics, crime reductions, and fund utilization.

SEC. 502. ACCOUNTABILITY PROVISIONS.

Federal officials who knowingly violate detention or enforcement provisions shall be subject to disciplinary action and loss of qualified immunity in appropriate cases.

SEC. 503. SEVERABILITY.

If any provision of this Act is held invalid, the remainder of the Act shall not be affected.

TITLE VI: GENERAL PROVISIONS

SEC. 601. AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.

There are authorized to be appropriated $25,000,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2032 to carry out this Act, with funds remaining available until expended.

SEC. 602. EFFECTIVE DATE.

This Act shall take effect 30 days after the date of its enactment.

**By Faith American Prosperity and Opportunity Act** 

A BILL 

To promote faith-informed American prosperity and opportunity by providing targeted support to veterans, servicemembers, low-income families, the unemployed, the homeless, the elderly, and all Americans seeking to achieve self-sufficiency and success in the 20th Congressional District of Texas and across the nation, through economic empowerment, workforce development, housing stability, education reform, veterans’ services, and faith-based partnerships.

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

(a) Short Title. This Act may be cited as the “By Faith American Prosperity and Opportunity Act” or the “By Faith PROSPER Act.”

(b) Table of Contents.

SECTION 2. FINDINGS AND PURPOSE.

Congress finds the following:

(1) The United States was founded on principles of faith, liberty, personal responsibility, and opportunity for all Americans, and reliance on God’s providence has historically guided the nation through challenges.

(2) In the 20th Congressional District of Texas (encompassing western San Antonio and parts of Bexar County), persistent poverty, unemployment rates around 4%, housing instability, challenges for veterans and the elderly, and barriers to economic mobility require targeted federal support that prioritizes American citizens and legal residents.

(3) Veterans and servicemembers have sacrificed for the nation and deserve priority access to housing, healthcare, job training, and reintegration services.

(4) Faith-based organizations, churches, and community groups have proven effective in delivering compassionate, results-oriented assistance to the poor, homeless, unemployed, and elderly, often at lower cost and with higher success rates than government programs alone.

(5) Socialism and government overreach have failed to deliver prosperity; instead, policies rooted in free enterprise, education choice, family values, and personal accountability lift individuals and communities.

(b) Purpose. The purpose of this Act is to:

Empower Americans in TX-20 and nationwide through opportunity-focused programs.

Expand support for veterans, soldiers transitioning to civilian life, the poor, the homeless, the unemployed, and the elderly.

Integrate faith-based and community partnerships.
Promote workforce development, housing, education, and economic growth.

Congress will appropriate necessary funds while encouraging private sector and charitable involvement.

SECTION 3. DEFINITIONS.

In this Act:

(1) “American” means a United States citizen or lawful permanent resident.

(2) “Faith-based organization” means a nonprofit organization with a religious mission that provides services without regard to recipients’ faith.

(3) “TX-20” means the 20th Congressional District of Texas.

(4) “Veteran” has the meaning given in section 101 of title 38, United States Code.

(5) “At-risk populations” include the poor, homeless, unemployed, elderly (age 65+), and families in TX-20 facing economic hardship.

TITLE I—ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT

SEC. 101. TX-20 Prosperity Grants.

(a) The Secretary of Commerce shall establish a grant program providing $250,000,000 annually for 5 years to states for distribution to TX-20 and similar districts for small business incubators, job training in high-demand fields (healthcare, trades, manufacturing, military transition skills), and micro-loans to American entrepreneurs.

(b) Priority to programs partnering with faith-based organizations and veteran-owned businesses.

SEC. 102. Expanded Earned Income Tax Credit and Opportunity Zones.

Enhance the Earned Income Tax Credit for low-income workers in high-poverty areas like parts of TX-20. Designate additional Opportunity Zones in economically distressed neighborhoods of Bexar County.

SEC. 103. Unemployment to Employment Bridge Program.
$100,000,000 for re-skilling and apprenticeships, with bonuses for hiring veterans and long-term unemployed.

TITLE II—VETERANS AND SERVICEMEMBERS SUPPORT

SEC. 201. Veterans Economic Empowerment Initiative.

(a) Authorizes $150,000,000 for expanded VA-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH) vouchers, prioritizing TX-20 veterans, including elderly and disabled veterans.

(b) Vocational rehabilitation and employment services tailored to combat medics, drill sergeants, and other military occupational specialties.

SEC. 202. Servicemember Transition Assistance.

Mandatory pre-separation job placement partnerships with private employers and faith-based mentorship programs.

SEC. 203. Major Richard Star Act Alignment.

Coordinates with existing efforts to ensure full benefits for medically retired veterans.

TITLE III—HOUSING AND HOMELESSNESS PREVENTION

SEC. 301. By Faith Housing Stability Fund.

$200,000,000 for grants to faith-based and community organizations providing emergency shelter, transitional housing, rapid re-housing, and permanent supportive housing, with emphasis on veterans and families in TX-20.

SEC. 302. Source of Income Protections.

Encourages states to prohibit discrimination against voucher holders (including veterans) in housing, building on local efforts in San Antonio.

SEC. 303. Elderly Housing Upgrades.

Grants for senior housing modifications, accessibility, and community centers.

Expands education savings accounts and charter school funding for TX-20 families. Prioritizes vocational training and parental rights.

Aligns with related legislation protecting children from harmful ideologies while supporting family stability programs.

TITLE V—FAITH-BASED AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS

"Lets get another can opened."  "Try to be more even in your filling - some of your cups are too short".  "Get more cups laid out but don't fill them till I tell you - we dont want to get too far ahead".

Last month U. S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins announced plans for a major reorganization of the U.S. Forest Service.

In a career in conservation that started as a teenager guiding musky fishing clients in Hayward, Mike went onto a long career in public lands that included serving as the Forest Service Chief from 1997 until 2001.  

The U.S. Forest Service has a long proud history with origins under President Teddy Roosevelt. The Forest Service today manages more than 193 million acres of our National Forests and Grasslands, including the more than 1.5 Million acre Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest here in Wisconsin. The Forest Service is the largest federal wildfire response agency, leads the world’s largest natural resources research agency, and supports state and local agencies involved in forest management and caring for trees in our cities.  

The recently proposed Forest Service reorganization, along with the President’s proposed 2027 budget for the Forest Service and his recent Executive Orders would all result in an agency severely reduced in scope, capacity, and funding.  Simply put, the Forest Service and its dedicated career professionals won’t be able to adequately care for our forests and all the benefits they provide if this reorganization goes through.      

This kind of reorganization was also explicitly prohibited without Congressional approval as recently as November 2025 with language in the USDA Appropriations bill.  And yet again, this Congress is sitting back, watching another agency decimated by the Project 2025 agenda.

Happy Veteran’s Day. On this snowy November morning, I sat down for coffee with my longtime friend, Doug. 

Doug's parents were my neighbors years ago in Baraboo, and Doug and I live near each other now in Chequamegon Bay. 

Doug is a disabled Air Force veteran. He served our country overseas supporting the diplomatic mission in Iraq. He served at home working for Federal Emergency Management Agency during Hurricane Katrina, and later as part of a team leading the response to the Swine Flu epidemic for the Centers for Disease Control. Doug is is still serving today as a Washburn firefighter and city councilman. 

When I asked Doug why he’s dedicated his life to public service, he laid out his belief as meaningfully and simply as I've ever heard: “Give before you take.” 

As a disabled vet, Doug depends on his VA health care to keep doing the work he loves. Lately, he’s been running up against delays and gaps in care that shouldn’t exist for anyone who’s done their duty. 

I believe in honoring that duty–not just with words, but with action. That means backing bipartisan legislation like the PACT Act, which expands VA care for toxic-exposed veterans. It means supporting bills such as the Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act, which passed the House with strong bipartisan support to make the VA more responsive and expand choice and support for veterans and caregivers. 

I’ll continue to support COLA adjustments to ensure benefits don’t shrink while costs rise, and I’ll push for rural-access initiatives that bring services to us–not make veterans chase them down. I’ll work to support every veteran in Wisconsin’s 7th, beacuse as Doug exemplifies, service doesn’t end when the uniform comes off–it begins again in our towns, our schools, and our fire halls. 

To all veterans: thank you for all you have given, and continue to give. And to my friend Doug, thank you for sharing your story, and for reminding me why this work matters.

I just enjoyed another Wisconsin Dairy Breakfast.  

While we recognize and celebrate Wisconsin’s dairy farmers, it’s worth asking what we’re doing to ensure a strong future for one of our most important industries, and one of our most recognizable ways of Wisconsin life.  

Since 1980, the farmer’s share of a basket of dairy products has fallen from about 50% to about 25% today. So while the big milk processors stay profitable, farmers' bottom lines suffer and we know that dairies today in too many years have production costs higher than what they sell their milk for. If you're losing $5 on every hundredweight of milk you just can’t make that up on volume. 

So it’s no secret why we’ve lost so many small and mid-sized farms and why so many farm towns have been hollowed out.

And since 2025, the administration’s tariff wars have made farm inputs even more expensive. The administration's chaotic and punitive tariffs practically overnight killed overseas export markets that took years and millions of dollars to establish for many farm products. 

Add to that this administration’s conflicting policies toward immigrants which large dairies depend on, which makes labor shortages even more challenging, and adds more unpredictability to running a large business.  

Farmers want good markets for their products, not just more bailouts. And farmers today need a Congress that gives more than just lip service to farming. 

So what’s the solution?  

We need to enforce and strengthen anti-trust laws to reduce the agri-business monopoly that keep farm prices below costs for farmers.

We badly need a trade policy that assures strong, stable markets for our farm products. 

We need to reform our agricultural visa system for immigrant workers in a way that meets the needs of today’s farms.

Thousands of people from all over Wisconsin enjoy Dairy Breakfasts every summer. If we want to assure that tradition then Congress needs to get to work to assure that farms like this one can be here for years to come.

I'm here on Thursday at Upper St. Croix Lake near Solon Springs. My eyes are burning, and if you're outside in northern Minnesota, Wisconsin, or Michigan right now your eyes are probably burning too. 

Millions of people across the northeastern U.S. have had to change their summer plans or are staying inside because of another season of massive fires that are now in the Boundary Waters of Minnesota and in Ontario.

If we think it's hard for us, think of the hundreds of U.S. Forest Service firefighters, and other firefighters from the U.S. and Canada working to contain these fires every day.

Our current Congressman, Tom Tiffany, posted yesterday blaming the increase in wildfires on "decades of fuel buildup in overgrown forests," claiming active forest management has been "sidelined by green lobby policies that lock up forests."

The fact is, after all these years, Tom Tiffany still doesn't get it. I'm a big proponent of forest management - in the right place at the right time - but we cannot log our way out of the growing problem of larger, more intense wildfires.

And if there's one thing we can be certain of, it's that with a changing climate, we are going to see more extreme heat like we've seen this week, more severe wind events, more flash floods, and more extreme wildfires like these in the years ahead. And we need to make the investments today to reduce those risks and respond to those events.

But Representative Tiffany has long been one of Washington's most dedicated zealots for disinvesting in the U.S. Forest Service and the other federal agencies that lead our responses to wildfires. In fact, last year Tiffany voted for a budget bill that rescinded funding for the very Forest Service programs that reduce wildfire fuel and protect old-growth forests, while mandating a sharp increase in commercial logging with no new resources to manage it safely.

This is exactly the wrong time to walk away from our investment in public lands and the people who care for them for ALL their benefits.

Climate change affects all of us, and it's not going to slow its acceleration without decisive, informed, bold action. Wisconsinites deserve a Congressman who understands what's at stake and who will tell the truth about what's happening to our air, water and land – and who isn't beholden to fossil fuel company lobbyists.

I want to go to Washington next year and help do that work for all of us. We'll get through this together if we work together.
